Orchestrator

The Orchestrator receives execution directives from the Conductor and owns the ordered traversal of Pipeline stages. It sequences configured Behaviors according to fixed Pipeline order, ensuring deterministic execution and isolation between Behavior effects within a .

The Orchestrator invokes only stages that are enabled, applicable, and configured with the instantiation. It does not make policy decisions, does not evaluate Controllers, and does not determine whether an attempt should proceed. Those responsibilities belong to the Conductor.

Orchestrator Responsibility

The Orchestrator is the execution engine for a 's Pipeline. Its responsibilities are narrowly scoped to stage traversal:

  • Stage sequencing — Behaviors are executed in their canonical Pipeline order. No stage may be skipped, reordered, or duplicated.
  • Isolation — Each Behavior receives an isolated copy of the current pipeline value. Mutations within a Behavior cannot affect upstream or downstream stages.
  • Determinism — Given identical state and configuration, the Orchestrator always produces the same result.
  • Error containment — Pipeline errors are captured, normalized, and dispatched through the error handling path without corrupting the state snapshot.

The Orchestrator does not enqueue attempts, does not evaluate Controllers, and does not manage the FIFO queue. It operates exclusively as a stage traversal engine.

Pipeline Stage Traversal

The Orchestrator traverses Pipeline stages in a fixed order. Each stage is occupied by zero or more Behaviors. Stages with no configured Behaviors are skipped silently.

Order Stage Role
1 Interceptors Intercepts the incoming value before resolution. May halt the Pipeline entirely.
2 Resolve Produces the State input from the incoming value, handling synchronous values, Promises, Observables, and HTTP resources.
3 Operators Applies transformations to the resolved value. May block the Pipeline by returning undefined.
4 Filter Filters State emissions based on configured filter functions.
5 BeforeTap Observation point before reduction. Receives an isolated snapshot of the current pipeline value.
6 Reducer Computes next State from the current pipeline value.
7 AfterTap Observation point after reduction. Receives an isolated snapshot of the reduced value.
8 Encrypt Applies encryption to the State before persistence.
9 Persist Persists the State to configured storage.
10 State Commits the final StateSnapshotShape and emits the resolved value through Signals and observable streams.
Replace vs Merge: The Orchestrator supports two operation modes. A Replace replaceState() operation resolves and commits a complete new State value. A Merge mergeState() operation resolves a partial value and combines it with the current State using the configured Merge Behavior before proceeding through downstream stages.
Value Isolation

The Orchestrator enforces strict value isolation between stages. Before each Behavior receives the pipeline value, it is deep-cloned. This prevents unintended mutation leakage between stages and guarantees that each Behavior operates on an independent copy.

After reduction completes, the final State value is cloned once more before being committed to the StateSnapshotShape. The pre-encrypted value is what consumers observe through Signals and streams. The post-encrypted value is what flows to persistence.

Error Handling

When a Behavior throws during Pipeline execution, the Orchestrator captures the error and routes it through a structured error path:

  • Normalization — The raw error is converted into an immutable Error representation.
  • Transform — Registered error transform Behaviors may reshape the error for consumer-specific needs.
  • State commit — The error is committed to the State snapshot so it is observable through Signals and streams.
  • Callbacks — Registered error callbacks are invoked with isolated copies of the error and the current snapshot.

Error handling does not interrupt queue processing. After error finalization, the Conductor advances to the next queued attempt.
